symptom: Motor trips, control panel indicates 'Phase Fault' or 'Motor does not start/runs rough'
problem_description: The three-phase power supply to the motor is either missing a phase or has an incorrect phase sequence, causing the control panel to trip the motor.
likely_causes: Blown fuse or tripped circuit breaker in one phase
Loose electrical connection in the power supply circuit
Utility power supply issue (missing phase)
Incorrect wiring of motor or control panel
understanding: The control panel's protection system detects an imbalance or incorrect sequence in the three-phase power supply, which can cause severe motor damage, and initiates a shutdown.
verify: Check all fuses and circuit breakers in the control panel and supply circuit
Measure voltage across all three phases at the control panel input with a multimeter
Verify phase sequence if motor runs rough but doesn't trip immediately
repair: Replace blown fuses or reset tripped breakers
Tighten all electrical connections
Contact utility provider if supply issue
Correct wiring as per connection diagram

symptom: Water leakage around pump connection
problem_description: The farmer observes water dripping or spraying from the joint where the pump's connector unit attaches to its support bracket.
likely_causes: Damaged or improperly seated rubber diaphragm
Loose connection bolts at the pump connector unit
Misaligned or damaged guide shoe
Debris caught in the sealing surface
understanding: The integrity of the 'leak proof joint' is crucial for pump operation, and any compromise in the rubber diaphragm, guide shoe, or connection tightness will lead to leaks and potential performance issues.
verify: Visually inspect the joint for obvious signs of damage to the rubber diaphragm or misalignment of the guide shoe.
Attempt to gently tighten the connection bolts to see if the leak stops or reduces.
repair: De-energize and depressurize the pump. Disassemble the joint, inspect and replace the rubber diaphragm if damaged. Clean sealing surfaces. Reassemble, ensuring the guide shoe is correctly positioned and all bolts are tightened securely.
